that-printer-of-udell-s-a-story-of-the-m: Harold Bell Wright's inspirational bestseller follows Dick Falkner, a penniless young printer's devil who rises through honesty, hard work, and faith. Set in a small Midwestern town, the story argues that character matters more than luck. Millions of readers took its message to heart, making Wright one of the most beloved moral storytellers of his generation.
the-children-of-the-new-forest: Captain Frederick Marryat's beloved children's classic hides four orphaned children of a Royalist officer in the New Forest during the English Civil War. Raised as the forester's grandchildren, they learn woodcraft, loyalty, and courage while danger lurks. One of the great adventure stories for young readers, loved for nearly two centuries.
lady-mary-and-her-nurse-or-a-peep-into-t: Pioneer author Catharine Parr Traill wrote this gentle book to introduce children to the wildlife of Canada. Through conversations between little Lady Mary and her nurse, young readers meet birds, beasts, and forest plants of the new world. Informative and tender, it opened young eyes to nature in the days before nature books were common.
the-suppressed-gospels-and-epistles-of-t: Archbishop William Wake's famous 1693 collection gathers the early Christian writings left out of the New Testament — gospels, epistles, and acts attributed to apostles and their followers. These apocryphal texts show how varied the first Christian centuries were. For readers curious about the roads the Bible did not take, this is the essential sourcebook.
the-people-of-the-mist: H. Rider Haggard — creator of King Solomon's Mines — sends his hero into the African interior in search of a lost white queen and her hidden people. Jungle perils, ancient mysteries, and Haggard's gift for the exotic drive the adventure. Classic lost-world fiction from the master of the genre.
woman-on-the-american-frontier-a-valuabl: William Fowler gathers the heroism of pioneer women — their endurance on the trail, their courage in Indian wars, their labor in building homes from wilderness. Drawing on letters and memoirs, he honors the women history books often forgot. A valuable, inspiring record of the frontier's unsung half.
lost-in-the-backwoods-a-tale-of-the-cana: Catharine Parr Traill — the beloved pioneer author — tells of children lost in the Canadian forest and their struggle to survive. Written from her own settler experience, the tale teaches woodcraft, courage, and trust in God. A classic of Canadian children's literature, still fresh and exciting.
lays-from-the-west: M. A. Nicholl's verses sing of the West — its pioneers, its landscapes, its legends — in ballad and lyric forms. Frontier poetry with heart and music, written when the West was still young. A voice from the days of the open range and the trail.
the-spanish-chest: Edna A. Brown's adventure centers on a mysterious Spanish chest — and the treasure, secrets, and perils locked inside it. Young heroes follow its clues through surprising twists toward a thrilling conclusion. A classic juvenile mystery-adventure in the best tradition of the genre, full of period charm.
beauty-and-the-beast: Madame de Beaumont's timeless tale — Beauty and her Beast, the enchanted castle, and the love that breaks the spell — in its classic form. The most beloved fairy tale ever told has charmed children for nearly three centuries. Every child should meet it here.
adventures-of-huckleberry-finn-chapters-: Tom Sawyer's elaborate plan to free Jim plays out in these closing chapters, with Huck as bewildered helper. When Jim's freedom is revealed as long settled, the boys light out — Huck for the Territory ahead. The end of the great American novel.
roving-east-and-roving-west: E. V. Lucas roves east and west — travel essays full of his urbane wit and keen observation. From English lanes to foreign cities, he is the perfect companion. A delightful book for armchair travelers. His civilized curiosity makes every place, from Kent to Cairo, a pleasure.
the-lincoln-story-book-a-judicious-colle: Henry Llewellyn Williams collects the best stories and anecdotes of Lincoln — his humor, his wisdom, his humanity. A judicious gathering from many sources. The Lincoln every American should know. Rail-splitting jokes and cabinet wisdom share these well-chosen pages.
first-and-last: Hilaire Belloc gathers essays first and last — on travel, inns, war, and the faith of Europe. His robust, rolling prose delights and provokes. Belloc at his most characteristic. Sussex downs, French inns, and Catholic faith recur in his rolling periods.
the-ancient-east: D. G. Hogarth's Ancient East surveys the lands of the Bible and the empires before Greece — Egypt, Assyria, and Persia in clear review. His learned, lucid account opened the field to general readers. A fine introduction to the old Orient and its wonders.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-sain: The Encyclopedia's Saint-Vaast entry: the Arras abbey of the apostle of Artois. Vaast's shrine drew the faithful. George Cyprian Alston gives its history. Old Flanders in monastic form. Its looms wove tapestries for half of Europe. Its abbots ruled a little state.
